newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch "unaware" of deal to name French ECB chief.
newsitem.headline: Dutch "unaware" of deal to name French ECB chief.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Thursday he was unaware of any Franco-German deal to appoint a Frenchman as first head of the European Central Bank and Dutchman Wim Duisenberg remained the best candidate.
"Neither I nor (foreign) minister (Hans) van Mierlo know of any such agreement," Dutch news agency ANP quoted Kok as saying.

Duisenberg, president of the Dutch central bank, is due to take over as president of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), forerunner of the European Central Bank (ECB), in July and had been widely expected to become the ECB's first president.
But French President Jacques Chirac said in December that Duisenberg would not automatically head the ECB.

Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli has said in a magazine interview that when it was decided to locate the ECB in Frankfurt there was an "unspoken commitment" by Germany that the bank's first president would be French.

The German magazine Wirtschaftswoche said this week that Frenchman Jacques Delors was an ideal candidate to head the ECB, adding that the choice would be made by France since Germany had won its fight to have the bank in Frankfurt.

Kok said the Netherlands stood squarely behind Duisenberg's candidacy. "Quality always shines through and Mr Duisenberg is an illustration of that. He will prove himself to be the best candidate, even to the French," ANP quoted him as saying.
